items.title: 52263_Sonny Greer oral history interview
items.q: Hawk and I were, for many years -- when it was Mamie Smith. ... Yeah. With a trumpet player... Hawk was in the band. That's the first time I saw Hawk, Lincoln(?) Theater, Mamie Smith, a very prominent singer.

ctx.x: Now, what bands do you think -- I wanted to ask you because I read once that Harry Carney said he remembered a battle of the bands in which Coleman Hawkins cut the whole Ellington band. Do you remember that?
No, never happened. Never happened. Hawk was at the top of the heap but he -- now, Hawk and I were, for many years -- when it was Mamie Smith.
Oh, with Mamie Smith and the Jazz Hounds?

items.title: 52263_Sonny Greer oral history interview
items.q: Mamie Smith, a very prominent singer. ... Yeah, she was something else.

ctx.x: Yeah. With a trumpet player, what was his name? He was a hell of a guy, Bubber had to cut him down to size. Johnny somebody. He'd play, he'd do a whole lot of -- Bubber ate him up. Bubber took his plunger and killed him. Hawk was in the band. That's the first time I saw Hawk, Lincoln(?) Theater, Mamie Smith, a very prominent singer.

Yeah, she was something else. But Hawk play in that side band? No way. 'Cause Bechet and Bubber and (Tricky), Bechet would take that napkin I was telling you about and put it -- and wash him away. No way in the world he could survive that. I wouldn't kid. He was good but he wasn't that good. And he knew it. And wasn't enough money in New York to make him buck our band. No way! Because we had some hot guys too, on that tenor sax. We had some tough guys. Oh, Ben was laying back there. Ben was playing -- he was…
